name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Rotate into the sector breakouts that are actually confirmed (regional banks on widening NIMs, biotech on M&A/catalyst momentum) and add the two mean-reversion legs the mandate always called for but the book never held -- long the statistically cheap, technically breaking-out gold miners and short the most stretched, richly-valued semis -- while dropping the two legs (broad healthcare, low-vol) that have just been dead weight with no confirmed catalyst.
reassessment_note: This book (-2.50% NAV, badly lagging SPY +3.62% and BTC +23.17% over the same stretch) has been sitting in four unconfirmed, half-committed positions -- KRE, XLV, XBI, USMV -- with no short leg despite a mandate that explicitly calls for gold-miner/semi mean reversion and a defensive-vs-discretionary pair. I rebuilt it around what the tape actually confirmed this week rather than what it was merely exposed to. Kept and increased KRE (20% -> 25%): regional banks are one of 2026's better financial trades, +9% YTD and +28% over a year on genuinely widening net interest margins as deposit costs roll over -- a confirmed breakout, not a hope. Kept and increased XBI (18% -> 22%): biotech is showing a real, catalyst-driven uptrend (post-conference data confirmations, sector momentum into a volatile but rising range), distinct from and stronger than broad healthcare. Dropped XLV (22% -> 0%): this is the unconfirmed leg -- XLV's 2026 story is dominated by Eli Lilly's GLP-1 pricing exposure and recurring drug-pricing/Medicare-Advantage-rate headwinds, and it has underperformed SPY by double digits this year with no fresh breakout catalyst; the mandate says rotate into confirmed moves, and XLV isn't one. Dropped USMV (7% -> 0%): the low-vol/defensive leg has just been a drag in a risk-on tape and was never actually paired against a discretionary short, so it wasn't expressing the relative-value idea the mandate names -- better to remove the unpaired half than keep bleeding on it. Added GDX long (13%): gold miners have broken through prior highs even as gold itself hasn't cleared its equivalent resistance (miners leading the metal, a classic leveraged-reversion setup), and GDX's free-cash-flow/EV yield is at record highs with forward multiples at five-year lows -- a legitimate mean-reversion-to-fair-value trade the book never held despite the mandate naming it explicitly (note: this book's one prior GDX attempt was stopped out, so sized modestly). Added SOXX short (10%): semis have pulled back 20% from June highs after a 250% run since April 2025, but SOXX still trades at ~76x trailing earnings and carries a Strong Sell valuation call even with the pullback -- the definition of the 'semi-extreme' the mandate was written to fade, funded by cutting XLV/USMV rather than raising gross materially. Cash raised slightly (33% -> 30%) reflects modestly higher gross exposure now that a real short leg is doing work instead of sitting idle.

positions.thesis: Increased from 20% to 25%. Confirmed sector breakout, not a hope trade: regional banks are +9% YTD and +28% over the past year as Q1-through-Q2 earnings confirm net interest margins widening as deposit costs roll over. This is the cleanest 'rotate into a confirmed breakout' leg in the mandate right now.

Increased from 18% to 22%. Biotech is showing a genuine catalyst-driven uptrend distinct from broad healthcare -- post-conference data confirmations have been driving sector momentum, and this is the specific sub-sector rotation the mandate targets rather than a defensive healthcare beta bet.

New leg, sized modestly given this book's prior GDX attempt was stopped out. Gold miners have broken through prior highs even though gold itself hasn't cleared the equivalent resistance yet -- miners leading the metal is the leveraged, mean-reversion-to-fair-value setup the mandate names explicitly, reinforced by GDX's free-cash-flow/EV yield sitting at record highs and forward EV/EBITDA at five-year lows.

New leg. This is the 'semi-extreme mean reversion' short the mandate was written for: SOXX ran 250% off its April 2025 low, has only pulled back 20% from June highs, and still trades near 76x trailing earnings with a Strong Sell valuation call despite continued inflows -- fade the extreme rather than chase the AI-capex momentum story that's already priced in.
